items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: I used to play snare drums sometimes with Tony Spago at the Dixieland Band and Biloxi in the Crockett Parade.

ctx.x: I used to play snare drums sometimes with Tony Spago at the Dixieland Band and Biloxi in the Crockett Parade. He'd say, Bruno, take my drums, I'm tired. He's playing with, he's with the original New Orleans Dixieland Jazz Band. He plays the kazoo.
Yeah, still in New York I guess, yeah.

items.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11
items.q: I was in Chicago just a couple years ago and I was with George Brunas' feelings every night, you know?

ctx.x: That's what George says. George says that himself. His brother is... Henry,

Henry had an awful lot of stuff. I think Henry today playing trombone on the street, then, playing like he played then right today would be a sensation. Henry played. I was in Chicago just a couple years ago and I was with George Brunas' feelings every night, you know? And he's playing fine. He's playing real good. Oh, Henry, Henry was a good trombone. But you see, you're going to go into that same old argument again. He wasn't a school musician like Edwards was.
You understand? He wasn't what you call a real hot man. No, he had a lot of stuff. He had good execution and all, you know? And he'd blow his head off. He took lessons from Dave Poikins.
